## Boundary mode

```text
[DECIDED 2026-09-04] MODE: NEW — foundation mode.

Cycle 0, the foundation feature (stack, scaffold, data layer, role switch,
deploy pipeline), runs WITHOUT an allow-list, because there is no host to
protect. Every later cycle treats the foundation as the host and inherits the
ordinary discipline: branch + flag + allow-list, additive only, stop-and-ask
for anything off-list.

THE TRIGGER, stated so it cannot be argued about later:

  The boundary switches ON the moment the first vertical slice runs end to end
  — an invoice created, approved, funded and disbursed, clickable, on a branch.

  Operationally: the first time `find . -name "page.tsx" | wc -l` returns
  non-zero AND that page is reachable, `discovery-kit/YOUR_PRODUCT.md` is stale
  and must be re-audited before the next Discovery. Its "Verify before
  trusting" block holds the exact commands.

After the trigger fires, cycle 0's output is host code. It stops being freely
editable and starts being something a later feature must justify touching.
```

## Framework rules

```text
[DECIDED 2026-09-04] Next.js (App Router) + Tailwind. Versions pinned at
scaffold in cycle 0; this line is rewritten with the exact versions then.

[DECIDED] Scale posture — say this plainly and do not let a later session
overstate it: THIS IS A DEMONSTRATION-SCALE SYSTEM. It is not built for volume
and does not need to be. Trade finance volume is low by web standards — 100K
invoices a day is ~1.2 writes/second, which a single Postgres instance answers
without effort. The risks in this domain are correctness, ordering, idempotency
and reconciliation, not throughput.

[DECIDED] The four seams that keep scale possible without building for it.
These are rules, not aspirations, and Design must reject a plan that breaks one:
  1. Ledger and settlement logic live in framework-free modules — never inside
     a route handler. (`receivables-financing-mvp/src/lib/pricing.ts` has this
     property, which is precisely why it is copyable.)
  2. Every money operation carries an explicit idempotency key.
  3. A webhook handler validates, persists and acknowledges. It does not
     process.
  4. Chain access sits behind an interface, so a worker owning nonce
     sequencing can replace it without touching domain code.
The extraction point — where a queue and worker would go — is named in the
case study rather than built.

[INHERITED — re-verify at scaffold] Next.js 16 is newer than most model
training data. `receivables-financing-mvp/AGENTS.md` opens with this warning and
the local docs live at `node_modules/next/dist/docs/`. Known divergences already
paid for in that repo: `middleware.ts` is `proxy.ts`; route `params` is a
Promise; `turbopack` and `outputFileTracingIncludes` are top-level, not under
`experimental`. Re-confirm against the version actually installed here.
```

## Data rules

```text
[DECIDED 2026-09-04] Postgres (Neon) + Drizzle. Every table in a migration in
this repository from the first commit.

That is a direct correction, not a preference. In `receivables-financing-mvp`
the migrations directory begins at 20260710 and `invoices`, `transactions` and
`profiles` predate it — the base schema was applied in a dashboard and exists
nowhere in version control, so its RLS state is unknowable from the repo. That
must not recur.

[DECIDED] Authorisation is ONE explicit layer, in application code. No
RLS-as-security-model. The sibling repo split it between the database and the
app and got a coarse "internal staff see everything" grant that its own
screen-permission system could not narrow.

[DECIDED] THE LEDGER — double-entry, beside an event log. Two tables, two jobs:
  settlement_events   what happened externally, WITH its proof
                      (tx hash · Circle payment id · statement line)
  ledger_entries      what it means financially, balanced, referencing that
                      evidence
Every movement is two or more entries summing to zero. **Balances are never
stored.** A balance is SUM(entries) for an account, always. Accounts include:
funder facility, platform treasury per token/currency, supplier payable,
unapplied cash, fees.

[DECIDED] MONEY IS INTEGERS IN MINOR UNITS. Never a float, never a JS number.
`receivables-financing-mvp` stores `transactions.amount` as `number` and its
verifier does `parseUnits(expectedAmount.toFixed(6), 6)` — a rounding surface
that is tolerable in a single-token demo and is not tolerable in a ledger.

[DECIDED] The boundary rule: feature-folder fixtures are typed from the
generated schema types (import type only); ZERO live database-client imports
inside a feature folder.
Audit command (rewrite the path once the client module exists):
  grep -rn "drizzle\|/db/client" src/features/<slug>/   → type imports only

[DECIDED] Schema changes: only what a design's data contract names, re-approved
before written.
```

```text
[DECIDED 2026-09-04] The demo has NO SIGN-IN. A visitor switches role rather
than authenticating — the property that makes the sibling agent-console demo
actually get used, where this app's ancestor could not be published at all.

[UNVERIFIED] The mechanism — how the active role is held and read, and how a
page asserts one — does not exist yet. Cycle 0 builds it and replaces this
block with the pattern and its file:line.

[DECIDED] Roles: supplier · funder · platform ops · debtor. The debtor surface
is public and unauthenticated by design, as an invoice payment link is in the
real world.
```

## Secrets and keys

```text
[AUDITED 2026-09-04] There are no secrets in this repo. No .env file of any
kind exists; `.gitignore` covers `.env` and `.env.*` with an `.env.example`
exception.

[DECIDED] This project calls NO model API. There is no ANTHROPIC_API_KEY and no
equivalent — it is not an AI product, and nothing here should acquire one
without a decision.

[DECIDED] Expected secrets, all server-side, read at request time, never
public-prefixed, never added to the host platform during Develop:
  CIRCLE_API_KEY        sandbox only
  CIRCLE_WEBHOOK_SECRET signature verification
  DATABASE_URL          Neon connection string

[AUDITED 2026-09-04] Circle sandbox access is live and was probed, not assumed.
Key held in `.env.local` (gitignored, verified); `SAND_` prefix, so it is a
sandbox credential and cannot move real money.

  Base URL   https://api-sandbox.circle.com
  Console    https://app-sandbox.circle.com/developer → API Keys

  GET /v1/configuration                → 200, masterWalletId returned
  GET /v1/businessAccount/balances     → 200, available [] unsettled []
  GET /v1/businessAccount/banks/wires  → 200, [] — no wire account registered
  GET /v1/payments · /v1/payouts · /v1/transfers · /v1/wallets · /v1/cards
                                       → 200 each

  Read-only GETs only; nothing was written. `/v1/ping` returns 404 — it is not
  a route on this API, so do not use it as a health check.

Two consequences for cycle 2, recorded now so they are not discovered late:
  - The sandbox returns 200 on every product surface. That is the sandbox being
    permissive, NOT proof the same products are enabled in production. Nothing
    here may claim production capability.
  - The account holds no balance and no registered wire account, so the fiat
    legs need a funded sandbox balance and a test bank account before any
    payment or payout call will do anything. That setup is cycle 2's first
    step, not a surprise in its middle.

The masterWalletId is deliberately NOT recorded in this file. It is specific to
one account, it is not a secret but it is not a stack fact either, and
`/v1/configuration` returns it on demand.

[DECIDED] Legitimately public vars (do not let their pattern bleed onto
secrets): the chain id, the public RPC URL, the explorer base URL, token
contract addresses, and any feature flag. All are public facts about a public
testnet.

[DECIDED] Chain id must be explicit and per-transaction, not a module constant.
`receivables-financing-mvp/src/lib/web3/usdc.ts:5` hard-codes it from
`wagmi/chains` while `NEXT_PUBLIC_CHAIN_ID` is declared and never read; a
multi-rail verifier cannot inherit that.
```

## Host platform and deploy posture

```text
[UNVERIFIED — Chetan to confirm from the dashboard once the project is linked]
Assumed Vercel, matching both sibling repos. No `.vercel/` directory exists
here yet and there is no git remote, so nothing about the deploy posture is
verifiable from this repo today.

What must be confirmed and written down before Deploy runs, per deploy-kit:
  - what a branch push actually causes (preview deployment, or nothing)
  - whether Preview and Production env scopes are separate
  - whether public vars are build-time inlined (if so, a change needs a redeploy)
  - whether SSO/deployment protection is ON by default — it was, in
    `kyc-agent-console`, and every URL redirected to a login wall until it was
    turned off. A portfolio demo behind SSO is invisible.

[DECIDED] The demo must deploy with NO secret that can cost money. That
property is what made the sibling agent console safe to leave open, and it is a
requirement here, not a nicety.

[DECIDED 2026-09-06] Repo and variant posture, Chetan's direction:
  - ONE public repo, licensed PolyForm Noncommercial 1.0.0 (LICENSE.md at
    root, fetched verbatim from polyformproject.org). Source-available:
    readable by anyone, commercial rights retained — the "sellable later"
    door stays open, and the sole author can relicense at will.
  - TWO deployments from that one codebase, never two repos: the public demo
    (role switch, no sign-in) and a login-gated accounts variant, selected by
    an AUTH_MODE env switch behind the getIdentity() seam (foundation design
    §6). The accounts variant is cycle 4a, slotted after the headline ships.
  - A private fork is explicitly rejected: it doubles integration work and a
    LICENSE file already provides everything privacy was meant to buy.
```

## The untouchables

```text
[AUDITED 2026-09-04] There is nothing to protect yet. No cron, no generated
types, no live schema, no auth.

[DECIDED] The list opens the moment cycle 0 lands, and these three are already
committed:
  - Applied migrations — never edited after the fact; corrections are new
    migrations. This is the specific failure the sibling repo has.
  - The ledger invariant — entries for a movement sum to zero, balances are
    derived and never stored. Any change to this is a decision, never a
    refactor.
  - `/discovery-kit/`, `/design-kit/`, `/develop-kit/`, `/deploy-kit/`,
    `/release-kit/` — the method layer, gitignored, edited only deliberately.
```

## High-stakes surfaces

```text
[DECIDED 2026-09-04] Everything this product does is high-stakes by the
template's definition — it moves money on every path. A human gate is mandatory
before:
  - a facility being committed, or drawn down
  - any disbursement to a supplier
  - any payout to a funder
  - applying a received payment to an invoice, where reconciliation is not an
    exact match
  - anything that would advance an invoice's state

[DECIDED] The gate rule, inherited deliberately from the sibling product and
worth restating: the browser posts DECISIONS, not RESULTS. A client's claim
about what happened is a hint about where to look, never evidence.
```
